Alpha 1.48.0 (less work, same world)

  • Equipped crowds: Compatible opaque character surfaces share frame-owned draw submissions. Animations, equipment, stealth, shadows and distant dungeon positions retain their appearance; unsupported surfaces keep normal rendering.
  • Town and woodland: Cached rigid transforms, compatible equipment surfaces, bounded scenery batches and conservative foliage culling reduce rendering work without removing visible detail or changing collisions.
  • Cleaner loading: The loading screen prepares two real initial-view frames, including shadows and postprocessing, before handing over controls. Removed an unconditional 1.1-second wait; cancelled entry cannot join a retired session.
  • Busy combat: Scene creation yields within its existing per-tick budget. Essential warnings retain FIFO delivery; compact remote feedback stays bounded while preserving local actions and healing feedback.
  • Measured, not promised: Controlled native-desktop equipped-scene and populated-world checks met their declared targets on High and Low. This is not a universal FPS or physical-phone guarantee. Progression, rewards and player saves are unchanged; earlier notes remain below.

Alpha 1.47.0 (steadier phone sessions)

  • Two-thumb control: Releasing or cancelling a skill aim no longer blocks the movement thumb's release. Repeated movement and aiming retain separate finger ownership, with no delayed compatibility-click cast.
  • Clean interruptions: Backgrounding, leaving the page, rotating, resizing, typing or opening phone menus clears held movement and pending skill aims. Connection recovery clears old local intent instead of replaying it; a fresh input is needed to continue.
  • Keyboard room: Native phone editors adapt open panels to the keyboard-sized visible screen, preserve horizontal centering and restore the original layout afterward. Thumb controls yield while typing; browser zoom and world-camera framing remain unchanged.
  • Safe skill focus: A pending aim cannot commit through open panels, account/chat fields or a disconnected/resuming session. Existing ally-targeting taps and ground-range limits remain.
  • Device review: Portrait/landscape browser gesture and keyboard-report checks passed. Actual phone combat and native-keyboard feedback remain player-playtest work; no synthetic phone-FPS or universal-device guarantee is claimed. Earlier notes remain below.

Alpha 1.46.0 (controls that fit you)

  • Your keyboard: Remap or unbind eighteen camera, ability and menu actions in Settings. Changes apply immediately and save per device, with conflict messages and a default reset. Escape, chat, browser navigation and mouse/modifier controls remain fixed; character builds and learned skills are unchanged.
  • Clear hints and safe focus: Hotbar keys, primary Help labels and nearby inspection prompts reflect your choices. Native account fields, selects and buttons keep their input without also casting abilities. Rebinding clears held camera input; unavailable browser storage is explained.
  • Less motion, essential information: Choose Always reduced or follow your device preference. Decorative wind, portal/courtyard motion, recoil, animated health changes, effects, casino celebrations and camera punches respect reduction. Danger boundaries, labels and timers remain; device reduction is never overridden.
  • Readable controls: Phone Play settings include the same binding and motion controls, alongside independent menu text size. The page no longer prohibits browser zoom; canvas pinch remains separate from menu gestures. The world canvas follows screen resizing without shrinking the phone UI. Menu shortcuts still work after interacting with bag slots, while focused controls cannot accidentally cast abilities. Existing audio controls and non-color warning cues remain available.
  • Honest limits: This is an accessibility baseline, not keyboard-only world play, universal accessibility or a photosensitivity safety guarantee. Final actors, assistive-technology feedback and the integrated quality review remain open. Full prior patch history is retained below.

Alpha 1.45.0 (clearer screens, calmer combat)

  • Combat stays readable: Wide desktop screens group health, mana and abilities in a compact central dock, with visible values and bindings. Persistent chat and wrapping menu controls leave room for combat; narrow and phone layouts retain their existing controls.
  • Manage your journey: Story and Contracts journal sections preserve tracking choices. Ready turn-ins appear first, progress is easier to read, and long quest lists keep their reading position. Minimap service names avoid icons and one another.
  • Inspect before acting: Desktop right-click or Shift+F10 opens scrollable item details and comparisons without equipping. Bag and Stash appear together on desktops with names, search, filters and capacity counts. Live refresh preserves reading position and focus.
  • See your build and costs: Wide character sheets place equipment beside stats, and Forge previews show upgrades and resource costs before spending. Capped items retain their stats with clear maximum-reached feedback. Inactive legacy equipment does not inflate comparisons or set counts.
  • Clearer results: Ground loot has separated, zoom-readable rarity labels; enemies retain targeting priority. Trading House reads show loading, empty and retry states without automatic purchases or retries, and opening sends only one search.
  • Progress preserved: Rewards, currencies, saved builds, pickup rules and server authority are unchanged. Accessibility, final actor assets and the integrated art-quality review remain open. Full prior patch history is retained below.

Alpha 1.44.0 (sound and atmosphere)

  • Your mix: Independent combat, interface and ambience controls are available in desktop/phone settings and saved per device. Master volume and mute apply consistently.
  • World atmosphere: Town, elemental realms, Dark Realm, dungeons and casino floors have distinct synthesized ambient beds with bounded crossfades. Instance identity takes precedence over reused world coordinates.
  • Recognizable actions: Fourteen short ability-family cast signatures distinguish steel, guard, shadow, fire, arcane, gravity, time, frost, healing and other actions. Danger cues use camera-relative direction while their visual warnings remain available with sound off.
  • Distinct contact: Confirmed physical, fire, cold, lightning, arcane, holy and shadow damage have short impact signatures. Bleed, poison and hazard ticks are quieter; zero-damage events and other players' unrelated fights do not add local hit sounds.
  • No stale sound pileup: Cue overlap is bounded with reserved danger capacity. Mute, hidden tabs, audio suspension and logout clear owned effects; returning restores eligible ambience without replaying missed combat sounds.
  • Polish continues: These are original code-generated sounds, not a finished cinematic score or final busy-fight listening approval. Combat values, timing, rewards and saves are unchanged; this does not open closed beta. Full prior patch history is retained below.

Alpha 1.43.0 (combat in motion)

  • Grounded class movement: All four classes' walks/runs make clearer foot contact, including equipped boots. Moving casts keep the lower-body stride while distinct upper-body gestures express attacks, spells and support.
  • Strikes with intent: Armed enemies swing toward their targets; creature gores, pecks, bites and thrusts have anticipation and recovery. Visible contact aligns with existing basic-attack timing, without changing damage or cooldowns.
  • Readable encounters: Wounded and selected enemy health bars follow the rendered actor and camera smoothly, with a clear damage-loss segment and phone/PvP targeting support. Friendly services do not receive enemy bars.
  • Quieter feedback and cleaner endings: Periodic damage/healing use smaller body-level cues. Enemy corpses hold their death pose and fade; corrected death poses stay above the floor. Reduced motion retains essential feedback.
  • Deployment reliability: Updated the game server's Pages proxy configuration to avoid unreachable IPv6 upstreams. Browser QA now reports the source of resource errors and the underlying navigation error without hiding failures.
  • Build security: Updated vulnerable brace-expansion build-tool dependencies to compatible patched versions; the dependency audit remains required.
  • Progress preserved: Skeleton rigid batching reduces redundant draws without dropping animated surfaces. Loot, movement speed, server respawn timing, saved builds and combat values are unchanged. Final authored actors and human combat-feel review remain open; this does not open closed beta. Full prior patch history is retained below.

Alpha 1.42.0 (a more grounded world)

  • Lanternhold rebuilt: Worn stone paving, constructed roofs and facades, market and smithy detail, planted seating and a clearer casino frontage. Replicated town fences no longer cover the new palisade with old orange boxes.
  • Roads worth exploring: Fuller woodland canopies, varied forest-floor beds, weathered trails and composed approaches connect the town, investigation sites and Bastion. The keeper's cottage, abandoned garden, Returning Scar, cold kiln and stranded wrecks have more distinct environmental storytelling.
  • Realm and dungeon identity: Water/Fire terrain and regional planting, rebuilt Molten/Abyssal/Tempest thresholds, Verdant crypt masonry and material relief across all five dungeon themes. Entrances agree with their reachable approaches; open realm crossings no longer expose a water stripe.
  • Grounded combat: Dungeon warnings and impact areas stay above the floor, Low/phone actors gain inexpensive contact shadows, and supporting contact/effect presentation follows the shared terrain surface. Reduced motion retains essential warnings.
  • Reliable typography: The game's heading font now loads with the game instead of depending on an external font service.
  • Performance and boundaries: Tighter scenery batches, culling and graphics-resource cleanup preserve essential visibility. Raised Earth terrain and rock-cover rules remain explicit QA-only options, not changes to the live world. High-scene performance and final modern-ARPG art acceptance remain open.
  • Progress preserved: No damage, cooldown, reward, currency, saved equipment or access rebalance. This does not open closed beta. Full prior patch history is retained below.

Alpha 1.41.0 (fitted class equipment)

  • Better-fitting outfits: Refined gloves, boots, shoulder armor, robes, helmets and hoods across all four classes. Leg equipment replaces both thighs and shins and bends at the knee; Rogue faces and hair remain visible under compatible headwear.
  • Connected details: Necklace chains, pendants, gems and weapon grips fit their rendered surfaces more closely. Fixed inward-facing shoulder armor and stale spell effects in the equipment preview.
  • Fewer character draw calls: Compatible rigid parts share draws while retaining animation joints, equipment visibility and stealth behavior. This is not a universal FPS guarantee.
  • Art work continues: These are improved procedural fallback models, not final authored character art or Diablo/PoE-quality acceptance. Character stats, saved equipment and collision sizes are unchanged; this does not open closed beta. Full prior patch history is retained below.

Alpha 1.40.0 (open-alpha playtest guide)

  • Goals in reach: Help → Open alpha now explains the first-dungeon, level-100, Dark Realm and finale pacing targets, plus Forge's long-term potency goal. These are playtest goals, not completed timing measurements.
  • Useful group feedback: The guide explains party preparation, manual quest claims, checkpoint returns and what class, time and assistance context makes a progression report useful. The optional timer remains off by default; nothing is submitted automatically.
  • Honest readiness: Published limits distinguish phone layouts from real-device dungeon/party testing and a planned beta population from proven concurrent capacity. Final modern character/world art and human balance review remain open.
  • Progress preserved: No XP, drop, reward, equipment or entry-rule changes. Existing accounts, characters and public alpha access continue; this update does not open closed beta. Full prior patch history is retained below.

Alpha 1.39.0 (progression playtest context)

Updated a development documentation dependency to its patched version, retaining the required security audit.

  • Compare the journey: The optional Help playtest timer now summarizes your class and active time in levels 1–29, 30–59, 60–99 and 100, along with solo and party roster sizes.
  • Useful, voluntary feedback: Hidden, disconnected, idle and suspended intervals stay separate. Party roster size does not prove participation, and outside help remains explicitly marked. The timer stays off until you start it; summaries stay local until you append them to a report draft and submit it.
  • Balance review continues: We are targeting roughly 2–3 hours to level 30, 100 hours to level 100 and 8–12 hours through the Dark Realm. Player campaign and balance playtests remain open; this update preserves existing rewards, rates, gear and saves.
  • Still open alpha: Current accounts and access continue. Full prior patch history is retained below.
